entries.mechanism: Forms intrastrand DNA cross-links like the alkylating agents.
entries.uses: Testicular, ovarian, lung, bladder, head and neck, cervical cancer; radiosensitiser.
entries.cautions: Markedly nephrotoxic, ototoxic and emetogenic — requires hydration and aggressive antiemesis; peripheral neuropathy; hypomagnesaemia.

entries.mechanism: As cisplatin with different toxicity profiles.
entries.uses: Ovarian, lung, breast (carboplatin); colorectal (oxaliplatin).
entries.cautions: Carboplatin is more myelosuppressive and less nephrotoxic; oxaliplatin causes distinctive cold-triggered peripheral neuropathy.

entries.mechanism: Masquerades as folate and jams DNA synthesis; toxicity can be rescued with folinic acid, which bypasses the blocked enzyme.
entries.uses: Leukaemia and lymphoma at high dose; rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and Crohn's at low weekly dose; ectopic pregnancy.
entries.cautions: It is a WEEKLY drug — accidental daily dosing has caused fatal marrow failure, a notorious medication error. Mucositis, hepatotoxicity, pneumonitis; teratogenic; interacts with trimethoprim and NSAIDs.

entries.mechanism: Inhibit thymidylate synthase, starving the cell of thymidine; capecitabine is an oral prodrug activated preferentially in tumour tissue.
entries.uses: Colorectal, breast, gastric and head-and-neck cancer; topical 5-FU for actinic keratosis.
entries.cautions: Mucositis, diarrhoea, palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia; catastrophic toxicity in DPD deficiency — now tested before treatment.

entries.mechanism: Incorporated into DNA as a false nucleotide, halting chain elongation; S-phase specific, so continuous infusion matters.
entries.uses: Acute myeloid leukaemia (the backbone agent); intrathecal for CNS leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Profound myelosuppression; cerebellar toxicity at high dose; a distinctive flu-like “cytarabine syndrome”; conjunctivitis requiring steroid drops.

entries.mechanism: Chain termination plus inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase — self-potentiating.
entries.uses: Pancreatic, bladder, ovarian and non-small-cell lung cancer.
entries.cautions: Myelosuppression; flu-like symptoms; haemolytic uraemic syndrome; radiation recall.

entries.mechanism: Converted to fraudulent nucleotides that halt purine synthesis and DNA replication.
entries.uses: Maintenance in acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; inflammatory bowel disease and autoimmunity (azathioprine).
entries.cautions: Check TPMT and NUDT15 activity before starting — deficient patients suffer catastrophic marrow failure. Allopurinol blocks their breakdown and multiplies toxicity.

entries.mechanism: Resist adenosine deaminase and incorporate into DNA, killing even resting lymphocytes.
entries.uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia; hairy cell leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Profound and prolonged lymphopenia with opportunistic infection; autoimmune haemolysis.

entries.mechanism: Supplies the tetrahydrofolate that methotrexate prevents the cell from making — bypassing the blocked enzyme rather than reversing the block.
entries.uses: Methotrexate rescue and toxicity; potentiates fluorouracil in colorectal cancer; with pyrimethamine.
entries.cautions: Note the opposite roles: it rescues from methotrexate but enhances fluorouracil. Never confuse with folic acid in these settings.

entries.mechanism: Binds acrolein in the urine, neutralising it before it damages the bladder — it has no anticancer action at all.
entries.uses: With cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide.
entries.cautions: Given on a schedule matched to the cytotoxic; omission causes haemorrhagic cystitis.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Bind tubulin and prevent microtubule assembly, so the mitotic spindle cannot form.
entries.uses: Leukaemia, lymphoma, sarcoma, lung and breast cancer.
entries.cautions: Vincristine causes peripheral neuropathy and is FATAL if given intrathecally — one of the most serious never-events in medicine; vinblastine and vinorelbine are more myelosuppressive.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: The mirror image of the vincas — they hyper-stabilise microtubules so the spindle cannot disassemble.
entries.uses: Breast, ovarian, lung and prostate cancer.
entries.cautions: Peripheral neuropathy; hypersensitivity reactions (premedicate with steroids and antihistamines); alopecia; docetaxel causes fluid retention.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Intercalate into DNA and poison topoisomerase II, generating free radicals.
entries.uses: Breast cancer, lymphoma, sarcoma, acute leukaemias.
entries.cautions: Distinctively cardiotoxic with a cumulative lifetime dose limit — echocardiographic monitoring; severe tissue necrosis on extravasation; red urine.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Generates free radicals causing DNA strand breaks; little marrow toxicity.
entries.uses: Testicular cancer, Hodgkin lymphoma.
entries.cautions: Pulmonary fibrosis — dose-limiting and worsened by high inspired oxygen, which anaesthetists must be told about.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Dactinomycin intercalates DNA blocking transcription; mitomycin alkylates and cross-links.
entries.uses: Paediatric sarcomas, gestational trophoblastic disease; bladder instillation and ophthalmic surgery (mitomycin).
entries.cautions: Severe vesicants; mitomycin causes haemolytic uraemic syndrome.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Stabilises the enzyme-DNA complex causing double-strand breaks.
entries.uses: Small-cell lung cancer, testicular cancer, lymphoma, HLH protocols.
entries.cautions: Myelosuppression; secondary leukaemia with a characteristic translocation.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Prevent religation of single-strand DNA breaks.
entries.uses: Colorectal (irinotecan); ovarian and small-cell lung cancer (topotecan).
entries.cautions: Irinotecan causes an acute cholinergic diarrhoea (treated with atropine) and a delayed severe diarrhoea; UGT1A1 polymorphism increases toxicity.

entries.subsection: Mitotic inhibitors, antibiotics and topoisomerase agents
entries.mechanism: Depletes circulating asparagine. Normal cells make their own; leukaemic lymphoblasts cannot, so they starve — a metabolic vulnerability rather than a DNA attack.
entries.uses: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Hypersensitivity (PEGylation reduces this), pancreatitis, thrombosis and bleeding from impaired hepatic protein synthesis, hyperglycaemia.

entries.mechanism: Blocks the abnormal fusion kinase driving chronic myeloid leukaemia — the landmark proof of concept that made targeted therapy a field, turning a fatal disease into a controllable one.
entries.uses: Chronic myeloid leukaemia; gastrointestinal stromal tumour; Ph-positive ALL.
entries.cautions: Oedema, cramps, rash, cytopenias; CYP3A4 interactions.

entries.mechanism: Bind the kinase in additional conformations, overcoming imatinib-resistant mutations.
entries.uses: Imatinib-resistant chronic myeloid leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Dasatinib: pleural effusion. Nilotinib: QT prolongation, vascular events. Ponatinib: arterial occlusion.

entries.mechanism: Block epidermal growth factor receptor signalling in tumours carrying activating EGFR mutations — which must be demonstrated first.
entries.uses: EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer, common in East and Southeast Asian populations.
entries.cautions: Acneiform rash (which correlates with response) and diarrhoea; interstitial lung disease.

entries.mechanism: Block B-cell receptor signalling.
entries.uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia; mantle cell lymphoma; Waldenström's.
entries.cautions: Atrial fibrillation, hypertension, bleeding tendency; newer agents are more selective with fewer cardiac effects.

entries.mechanism: Block cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, arresting the cell cycle at the G1 checkpoint.
entries.uses: Hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer with endocrine therapy.
entries.cautions: Neutropenia (usually manageable); ribociclib prolongs QT; abemaciclib causes diarrhoea.

entries.mechanism: Block single-strand break repair; in BRCA-mutant cells lacking homologous recombination this is synthetically lethal — killing only cells that already carry the defect.
entries.uses: BRCA-mutated ovarian, breast, prostate and pancreatic cancer.
entries.cautions: Anaemia, fatigue, nausea; secondary myeloid malignancy.

entries.mechanism: Block VEGF and other receptor kinases, starving the tumour of new blood vessels.
entries.uses: Renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, thyroid cancer, sarcoma.
entries.cautions: Hypertension, hand-foot syndrome, proteinuria, impaired wound healing, hypothyroidism.

entries.mechanism: Block the constitutively active BRAF V600E kinase and the downstream MEK node; combining them delays resistance and reduces skin toxicity.
entries.uses: BRAF-mutant melanoma; some lung and thyroid cancers.
entries.cautions: Photosensitivity, pyrexia, secondary cutaneous squamous carcinomas with BRAF inhibitor alone.

entries.mechanism: Restores apoptosis by blocking the anti-apoptotic BCL-2 protein that leukaemic cells rely on to survive.
entries.uses: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia; acute myeloid leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Tumour lysis syndrome — requires careful dose ramp-up and hydration.

entries.mechanism: Block the proteasome that degrades ubiquitinated proteins. Myeloma cells produce vast quantities of immunoglobulin and depend on rapid protein clearance, so they are uniquely vulnerable to the resulting misfolded-protein stress.
entries.uses: Multiple myeloma; mantle cell lymphoma.
entries.cautions: Painful peripheral neuropathy (much less with subcutaneous bortezomib); herpes zoster reactivation — aciclovir prophylaxis; carfilzomib is cardiotoxic.

entries.mechanism: Bind cereblon and redirect an E3 ubiquitin ligase to destroy transcription factors the myeloma cell needs — targeted protein degradation rather than inhibition.
entries.uses: Multiple myeloma; myelodysplasia with 5q deletion; erythema nodosum leprosum.
entries.cautions: Catastrophically teratogenic — thalidomide caused the defining disaster of modern drug regulation, and pregnancy prevention programmes remain mandatory. High VTE risk requiring prophylaxis; neuropathy with thalidomide.

entries.drug: All-trans retinoic acid (tretinoin) and arsenic trioxide
entries.mechanism: Rather than killing the cell, they force the blocked promyelocyte to mature into a normal neutrophil — differentiation therapy, and the reason acute promyelocytic leukaemia went from most lethal to most curable leukaemia.
entries.uses: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia.
entries.cautions: Differentiation syndrome — fever, dyspnoea, hypotension and pulmonary infiltrates, treated with dexamethasone; arsenic prolongs QT.

entries.mechanism: Block the mTOR kinase controlling cell growth and proliferation.
entries.uses: Renal cell carcinoma; breast cancer; subependymal giant cell astrocytoma; transplant.
entries.cautions: Mouth ulcers, hyperglycaemia, hyperlipidaemia, pneumonitis, impaired wound healing.

entries.mechanism: Binds CD20 on B-cells and depletes them by complement-and cell-mediated killing.
entries.uses: B-cell lymphoma and leukaemia; rheumatoid arthritis, ANCA vasculitis, MS, membranous nephropathy.
entries.cautions: Infusion reactions; hepatitis B reactivation — screen first, a particular concern given high hepatitis B prevalence across Asia; prolonged hypogammaglobulinaemia.

entries.mechanism: Binds the HER2 receptor over-expressed in some breast and gastric cancers — meaning it only helps patients whose tumour carries the target, which is why tumours are tested first.
entries.uses: HER2-positive breast and gastric cancer.
entries.cautions: Cardiotoxicity — a fall in ejection fraction, usually reversible; monitored by echocardiography, compounded by anthracyclines.

entries.mechanism: Do not attack the tumour at all — they block the molecular brakes tumours use to switch off T-cells, unleashing the patient's own immune system.
entries.uses: Melanoma, lung, renal, bladder, head-and-neck, cervical and mismatch-repair-deficient tumours.
entries.cautions: Immune-related adverse events — colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, thyroid and pituitary dysfunction — treated with steroids, not dose reduction. A genuinely different toxicity paradigm.

entries.mechanism: Blocks CTLA-4, releasing an earlier brake on T-cell priming.
entries.uses: Melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, often combined with a PD-1 agent.
entries.cautions: Higher rate of severe immune toxicity than PD-1 agents, especially colitis and hypophysitis.

entries.mechanism: Neutralises vascular endothelial growth factor, inhibiting tumour angiogenesis.
entries.uses: Colorectal, lung, ovarian and renal cancer; intravitreal use in macular degeneration.
entries.cautions: Hypertension, proteinuria, impaired wound healing, GI perforation, bleeding.

entries.mechanism: One arm grips CD19 on the leukaemic B-cell, the other grips CD3 on a T-cell, physically forcing the two together so the T-cell kills a target it never recognised.
entries.uses: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, especially measurable residual disease.
entries.cautions: Cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity; requires continuous infusion over weeks.

entries.drug: Trastuzumab emtansine / brentuximab vedotin / enfortumab vedotin
entries.mechanism: Use an antibody as a delivery vehicle to carry a potent cytotoxic directly to target-bearing cells.
entries.uses: HER2-positive breast cancer; CD30-positive lymphoma; urothelial cancer.
entries.cautions: Combine antibody and cytotoxic toxicities; neuropathy, thrombocytopenia, hepatotoxicity.

entries.mechanism: The patient's own T-cells are engineered to express a receptor against CD19 and reinfused.
entries.uses: Refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and lymphoma.
entries.cautions: Cytokine release syndrome (treated with tocilizumab) and neurotoxicity; specialist centres only.

entries.mechanism: Blocks oestrogen receptors in breast tissue while activating them in bone and uterus — one molecule, opposite effects in different tissues.
entries.uses: Oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer, treatment and prevention.
entries.cautions: Endometrial cancer and VTE risk (from its uterine agonism); hot flushes. Requires CYP2D6 activation — avoid strong CYP2D6 inhibitors such as paroxetine.

entries.mechanism: Block peripheral conversion of androgens to oestrogens, removing the residual postmenopausal oestrogen supply.
entries.uses: ER-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women.
entries.cautions: Arthralgia, bone loss and fracture, hot flushes; ineffective before menopause unless ovarian function is suppressed.

entries.mechanism: Block androgen binding; enzalutamide also blocks nuclear translocation.
entries.uses: Prostate cancer, including castration-resistant disease.
entries.cautions: Gynaecomastia; enzalutamide causes fatigue and seizures; flutamide is hepatotoxic.

entries.mechanism: Blocks androgen synthesis in testis, adrenal and tumour tissue.
entries.uses: Metastatic prostate cancer, with prednisolone.
entries.cautions: Mineralocorticoid excess — hypertension, hypokalaemia, fluid retention; hepatotoxicity.

entries.mechanism: Binds cyclophilin and inhibits calcineurin, blocking IL-2 transcription and hence T-cell activation.
entries.uses: Transplant rejection prevention; severe psoriasis, eczema, ulcerative colitis; dry eye (topical).
entries.cautions: Narrow therapeutic index with level monitoring; nephrotoxicity, hypertension, gum hypertrophy, hirsutism, tremor; heavily CYP3A4-dependent.

entries.mechanism: Binds FKBP-12 to inhibit calcineurin — the same end point as ciclosporin, more potently.
entries.uses: Transplant immunosuppression; topically for atopic eczema.
entries.cautions: Nephrotoxicity, tremor, post-transplant diabetes; monitored levels; CYP3A4 interactions.

entries.mechanism: Converted to 6-mercaptopurine, incorporated into DNA, suppressing lymphocyte proliferation.
entries.uses: Transplant; autoimmune hepatitis, IBD, vasculitis; steroid sparing.
entries.cautions: Marrow suppression — check TPMT/NUDT15 before starting; catastrophic interaction with allopurinol; hepatitis; skin cancer risk.

entries.mechanism: Blocks de novo purine synthesis, on which lymphocytes uniquely depend.
entries.uses: Transplant; lupus nephritis; vasculitis.
entries.cautions: GI upset, marrow suppression; strongly teratogenic — pregnancy prevention mandatory.

entries.mechanism: Blocks the mammalian target of rapamycin, arresting lymphocyte proliferation.
entries.uses: Transplant, sparing calcineurin nephrotoxicity; drug-eluting stents; lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
entries.cautions: Impaired wound healing, mouth ulcers, hyperlipidaemia, pneumonitis.

entries.mechanism: Basiliximab blocks the IL-2 receptor alpha chain on activated T-cells; ATG depletes T-cells outright.
entries.uses: Induction at the time of transplantation, when rejection risk is highest.
entries.cautions: ATG causes cytokine release, serum sickness and profound prolonged lymphopenia.

entries.mechanism: Raises lysosomal pH, impairing antigen processing and toll-like receptor signalling.
entries.uses: Systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, Sjögren's.
entries.cautions: Retinal toxicity with cumulative dose — annual screening after five years.

entries.mechanism: Blocks dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, limiting lymphocyte proliferation.
entries.uses: Rheumatoid and psoriatic arthritis.
entries.cautions: Hypertension, hepatotoxicity, very long half-life needing cholestyramine washout; teratogenic.

entries.mechanism: Prevents neutrophil migration and inflammasome activation.
entries.uses: Familial Mediterranean fever; pericarditis; Behçet's.
entries.cautions: Diarrhoea; myopathy with statins; narrow margin in renal impairment.

entries.mechanism: Neutralise tumour necrosis factor, a master switch of inflammation. Etanercept is a soluble receptor decoy rather than an antibody.
entries.uses: Rheumatoid, psoriatic and axial spondyloarthritis; Crohn's and ulcerative colitis; psoriasis; uveitis.
entries.cautions: Serious infection and reactivation of latent tuberculosis — screening is mandatory, and matters greatly in high-TB-prevalence regions; demyelination; worsening heart failure; drug-induced lupus.

entries.mechanism: Blocks interleukin-6 signalling.
entries.uses: Rheumatoid arthritis; giant cell arteritis; cytokine release syndrome after CAR-T.
entries.cautions: Infection; it suppresses CRP so infection markers become unreliable; GI perforation; deranged lipids.

entries.mechanism: Block the cytokine axes driving psoriatic inflammation.
entries.uses: Psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease (IL-23 agents).
entries.cautions: Infection; anti-IL-17 agents can worsen inflammatory bowel disease and cause candidiasis.

entries.mechanism: A CTLA-4 fusion protein blocking the second signal T-cells need for activation.
entries.uses: Rheumatoid arthritis.
entries.cautions: Infection risk; infusion reactions.

entries.mechanism: Small molecules blocking intracellular JAK-STAT signalling downstream of many cytokine receptors — oral, unlike the biologics.
entries.uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, ulcerative colitis, atopic eczema, alopecia areata.
entries.cautions: Herpes zoster reactivation, venous thromboembolism, cardiovascular events and malignancy in older patients — regulatory restrictions apply.

entries.mechanism: Block terminal complement activation.
entries.uses: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria; atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome; myasthenia gravis; NMOSD.
entries.cautions: Meningococcal infection risk — vaccination and prophylactic antibiotics are mandatory.

entries.mechanism: Binds interferon receptors triggering antiviral and antiproliferative gene programmes — borrowing the body's own antiviral signalling.
entries.uses: Chronic hepatitis B and D; some myeloproliferative neoplasms; Kaposi sarcoma.
entries.cautions: Severe flu-like symptoms, depression and suicidality, cytopenias, thyroid dysfunction, autoimmune flare. Largely displaced in hepatitis C by direct-acting antivirals.

entries.mechanism: Exchange potassium for calcium or sodium in the gut lumen, removing potassium from the body rather than merely shifting it into cells — which is what insulin and salbutamol do.
entries.uses: Chronic hyperkalaemia; enabling continuation of ACE inhibitors and mineralocorticoid antagonists in heart failure and CKD.
entries.cautions: Hypomagnesaemia (patiromer); sodium load and oedema (zirconium); they bind other drugs — separate dosing.

entries.mechanism: Older potassium-binding resin exchanging potassium for calcium in the colon.
entries.uses: Hyperkalaemia.
entries.cautions: Constipation and rare intestinal necrosis; slow onset makes it useless in an emergency.

entries.mechanism: Bind dietary phosphate in the gut so it is never absorbed — taken with food, since that is when phosphate arrives.
entries.uses: Hyperphosphataemia in chronic kidney disease and dialysis.
entries.cautions: GI upset; sevelamer also lowers LDL. A binder taken at the wrong time is a placebo — timing is the whole treatment.

entries.mechanism: Bind phosphate in the gut lumen while also supplying calcium.
entries.uses: Hyperphosphataemia where calcium loading is acceptable.
entries.cautions: Vascular calcification with cumulative calcium load; hypercalcaemia.

entries.mechanism: Buffers the metabolic acidosis of failing kidneys, which otherwise drives bone and muscle loss.
entries.uses: Metabolic acidosis of chronic kidney disease; urinary alkalinisation.
entries.cautions: Sodium load worsening hypertension and oedema.

entries.mechanism: A glucose or icodextrin osmotic gradient across the peritoneum removes water and solute — using the patient's own membrane as the dialyser.
entries.uses: Renal replacement therapy, especially where haemodialysis access is limited.
entries.cautions: Peritonitis; glucose absorption causing hyperglycaemia and weight gain; encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis.

entries.mechanism: Distributes through the extracellular space; roughly a quarter remains intravascular.
entries.uses: Resuscitation, replacement and maintenance fluid therapy.
entries.cautions: Large volumes cause hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis; fluid overload.

entries.mechanism: As saline with a more physiological electrolyte and buffer composition.
entries.uses: Resuscitation and maintenance; increasingly preferred over saline.
entries.cautions: Contains potassium — caution in hyperkalaemia; lactate metabolism impaired in liver failure.

entries.mechanism: Once glucose is metabolised only water remains, which distributes through total body water.
entries.uses: Free water replacement; hypoglycaemia (concentrated forms); vehicle for infusions.
entries.cautions: NOT a resuscitation fluid — little stays intravascular; hyponatraemia if used for maintenance alone.

entries.mechanism: Provides oncotic pressure and binds and transports numerous substances.
entries.uses: Large-volume paracentesis; spontaneous bacterial peritonitis; hepatorenal syndrome.
entries.cautions: No mortality advantage over crystalloid in general resuscitation, and harmful in traumatic brain injury — physiological plausibility is not evidence.

entries.mechanism: Large molecules that remain intravascular, expanding plasma volume.
entries.uses: Plasma volume expansion where blood products are unavailable.
entries.cautions: Hydroxyethyl starch causes renal failure and death and is now restricted; dextran impairs coagulation and causes anaphylaxis.

entries.mechanism: Restores intracellular and extracellular potassium.
entries.uses: Hypokalaemia.
entries.cautions: Concentrated IV potassium is fatal if given as a bolus — always diluted and rate-controlled; oral forms irritate the gut.

entries.mechanism: Antagonises potassium's effect on the cardiac membrane, restoring the threshold potential — it does nothing to the potassium level itself.
entries.uses: Hyperkalaemia with ECG changes; hypocalcaemia; calcium channel blocker overdose; hydrofluoric acid burns; magnesium toxicity.
entries.cautions: Tissue necrosis on extravasation (worse with chloride); do not mix with bicarbonate.

entries.mechanism: Cofactor for hundreds of enzymes and a membrane stabiliser.
entries.uses: Hypomagnesaemia; eclampsia; torsades; severe asthma.
entries.cautions: Loss of deep tendon reflexes signals toxicity; renally cleared.

entries.drug: Oral rehydration salts and ready-to-use therapeutic food
entries.mechanism: ORS exploits sodium-glucose cotransport; RUTF provides energy-dense nutrition without needing water or refrigeration.
entries.uses: Diarrhoeal dehydration; severe acute malnutrition.
entries.cautions: RUTF must be introduced cautiously to avoid refeeding syndrome.

entries.mechanism: Supplies amino acids, glucose, lipid, electrolytes, vitamins and trace elements directly, bypassing the gut entirely.
entries.uses: Intestinal failure where enteral feeding is impossible.
entries.cautions: Refeeding syndrome — give thiamine and monitor phosphate, potassium and magnesium closely; line sepsis; hepatic steatosis.

entries.mechanism: Chelates copper into an excretable complex and depletes tissue stores.
entries.uses: Wilson's disease; cystinuria; lead and mercury poisoning.
entries.cautions: Marrow suppression, nephrotic syndrome, myasthenia, drug-induced lupus; pyridoxine supplementation needed.

entries.mechanism: Trientine chelates copper; zinc induces intestinal metallothionein which traps dietary copper inside enterocytes.
entries.uses: Wilson's disease, treatment and maintenance.
entries.cautions: Better tolerated than penicillamine; zinc causes gastric irritation.

entries.mechanism: Sulfhydryl or carboxyl groups bind metal ions more avidly than tissue proteins do, forming excretable complexes.
entries.uses: Lead, arsenic, mercury and gold poisoning.
entries.cautions: Dimercaprol is given in peanut oil by painful injection and can redistribute metal to the brain; succimer is the oral alternative.

entries.mechanism: Traps caesium and thallium in the gut, interrupting enterohepatic recirculation.
entries.uses: Radioactive caesium and thallium poisoning.
entries.cautions: Constipation; blue stools; stockpiled for radiological incidents.

entries.mechanism: Provide alternative pathways for waste nitrogen excretion, bypassing the blocked urea cycle.
entries.uses: Urea cycle disorders with hyperammonaemia.
entries.cautions: Nausea, unpleasant odour; electrolyte disturbance.

entries.mechanism: Nitisinone blocks an upstream enzyme to prevent toxic metabolite formation; sapropterin is a BH4 cofactor rescuing residual enzyme activity.
entries.uses: Hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1; BH4-responsive phenylketonuria.
entries.cautions: Dietary restriction remains essential alongside both.

entries.mechanism: Supply the deficient lysosomal enzyme by infusion, taken up via mannose-6-phosphate receptors.
entries.uses: Gaucher, Fabry and mucopolysaccharidose disorders.
entries.cautions: Anti-drug antibodies reduce efficacy; they do not cross the blood-brain barrier, so neurological disease progresses untreated.

entries.mechanism: Nusinersen redirects SMN2 splicing; onasemnogene delivers a working SMN1 gene by viral vector; patisiran silences transthyretin mRNA.
entries.uses: Spinal muscular atrophy; hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
entries.cautions: Nusinersen needs repeated intrathecal dosing; onasemnogene causes hepatotoxicity and cannot be used if anti-vector antibodies exist.

entries.mechanism: Increase uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humour. First-line in glaucoma.
entries.uses: Open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension.
entries.cautions: Permanent iris and periocular skin darkening and eyelash lengthening — warn the patient, especially with unilateral treatment; conjunctival hyperaemia.

entries.mechanism: Reduces aqueous production by the ciliary epithelium.
entries.uses: Glaucoma.
entries.cautions: Systemically absorbed through the nasolacrimal duct — can cause bronchospasm, bradycardia and masked hypoglycaemia. Punctal occlusion reduces this.

entries.mechanism: Reduce aqueous humour formation.
entries.uses: Glaucoma, usually as add-on or in combination with timolol.
entries.cautions: Bitter taste, stinging; sulfonamide-type reactions.

entries.mechanism: Reduce aqueous production and increase outflow.
entries.uses: Glaucoma.
entries.cautions: Allergic conjunctivitis; avoid in infants (CNS depression and apnoea).

entries.mechanism: Constricts the pupil, pulling the iris away from the trabecular meshwork.
entries.uses: Acute angle-closure glaucoma; presbyopia.
entries.cautions: Brow ache, dim vision, retinal detachment risk in myopes.

entries.mechanism: Block iris sphincter and ciliary muscle, dilating the pupil and paralysing accommodation.
entries.uses: Fundoscopy; uveitis (to prevent synechiae); cycloplegic refraction in children.
entries.cautions: Blurred near vision for hours; can precipitate acute angle-closure in susceptible eyes; do not drive afterwards.

entries.mechanism: Local ribosomal inhibition.
entries.uses: Bacterial conjunctivitis.
entries.cautions: Local irritation; systemic toxicity essentially theoretical by this route.

entries.mechanism: Injected directly into the vitreous to block VEGF-driven abnormal vessel growth and leakage — confining a systemically active drug to one organ.
entries.uses: Wet age-related macular degeneration; diabetic macular oedema; retinal vein occlusion.
entries.cautions: Endophthalmitis and retinal detachment from injection; small systemic thromboembolic signal.

entries.mechanism: Local suppression of ocular inflammation.
entries.uses: Uveitis; post-operative inflammation.
entries.cautions: Raised intraocular pressure (steroid responders), cataract, and worsening of herpes simplex keratitis — never use on an undiagnosed red eye.

entries.mechanism: Local nuclear receptor action suppressing cutaneous inflammation; potency graded from mild to very potent.
entries.uses: Eczema, psoriasis, contact dermatitis, lichen planus.
entries.cautions: Skin atrophy, striae, telangiectasia, perioral dermatitis; systemic absorption from potent steroids over large areas. Match potency to site — mild on the face, potent on palms.

entries.mechanism: Restore the lipid barrier and reduce transepidermal water loss; urea additionally hydrates and keratolyses.
entries.uses: The foundation of all eczema and dry skin care.
entries.cautions: Paraffin-based products are a fire hazard on clothing and bedding.

entries.mechanism: Binds vitamin D receptors to normalise keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation.
entries.uses: Chronic plaque psoriasis, often combined with a topical steroid.
entries.cautions: Local irritation; hypercalcaemia if large amounts are used.

entries.mechanism: Reduce epidermal turnover and remove scale.
entries.uses: Psoriasis; scalp conditions; wart treatment (salicylic acid).
entries.cautions: Staining, irritation and odour limit adherence; dithranol burns normal skin.

entries.mechanism: Shrinks sebaceous glands, reduces sebum and normalises follicular keratinisation.
entries.uses: Severe nodulocystic or scarring acne.
entries.cautions: Severe teratogen — pregnancy prevention programme with two contraceptive methods and regular testing; dryness, deranged lipids and LFTs; mood monitored.

entries.mechanism: Normalise follicular keratinisation and comedone formation.
entries.uses: Acne; photoageing.
entries.cautions: Irritation, photosensitivity; avoid in pregnancy.

entries.mechanism: Releases free radicals that kill Cutibacterium acnes without generating resistance.
entries.uses: Acne, usually combined with a topical antibiotic to limit resistance.
entries.cautions: Irritation; bleaches fabric and hair.

entries.mechanism: Inhibits tyrosinase, reducing melanin synthesis.
entries.uses: Melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation — common indications across Asian dermatology.
entries.cautions: Paradoxical exogenous ochronosis with prolonged use; irritation; restricted or banned in some countries.

entries.mechanism: Silver ions and sulfonamide action; permanganate is an oxidising astringent.
entries.uses: Burns; exudative or infected eczema.
entries.cautions: Silver causes neutropenia and argyria; permanganate stains skin and nails brown.

entries.mechanism: Zinc and ferric oxides give a mild astringent and cooling effect as the suspension evaporates — largely physical rather than pharmacological.
entries.uses: Pruritus, mild sunburn, chickenpox, insect bites.
entries.cautions: No evidence of an active antipruritic mechanism, but cheap, safe and long established.

entries.mechanism: Binds tubulin and arrests dividing keratinocytes in metaphase, destroying wart tissue.
entries.uses: Anogenital warts.
entries.cautions: Severely teratogenic and neurotoxic if absorbed — strictly limited application area, never in pregnancy; podophyllotoxin is the purified, safer self-applied form.

entries.mechanism: Blocks bacterial folate synthesis on the skin surface; sulfur is keratolytic and mildly antimicrobial.
entries.uses: Acne, rosacea, seborrhoeic dermatitis.
entries.cautions: Sulfonamide hypersensitivity; unpleasant odour limits adherence.

entries.mechanism: Absorbs or reflects UVA and UVB before it reaches the skin.
entries.uses: Photosensitivity disorders; albinism; prevention of skin cancer and photoageing; mandatory with photosensitising drugs.
entries.cautions: Needs generous and repeated application to achieve labelled SPF.

entries.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid action on nasal mucosa with minimal systemic exposure.
entries.uses: Allergic rhinitis; nasal polyps.
entries.cautions: Epistaxis, nasal irritation; aim the spray away from the septum.

entries.drug: Transdermal patches (fentanyl, buprenorphine, rivastigmine, nicotine, oestradiol, hyoscine)
entries.mechanism: Steady absorption across skin, bypassing first-pass metabolism and giving stable levels for days.
entries.uses: Chronic stable pain, dementia, smoking cessation, HRT, motion sickness.
entries.cautions: Slow onset and offset; heat increases absorption dangerously (fentanyl with fever or hot baths); always remove the old patch.

entries.drug: Intrathecal and epidural agents (bupivacaine, morphine, baclofen)
entries.mechanism: Delivered directly into or around the spinal canal, bypassing the blood-brain barrier so tiny doses suffice.
entries.uses: Spinal and epidural anaesthesia; refractory pain; severe spasticity.
entries.cautions: High-risk route; drugs given by the wrong route here are lethal — vincristine being the notorious example.

entries.mechanism: Excreted into urine where it exerts a direct local analgesic effect on the urothelium — it is not an antibiotic and does not treat the infection.
entries.uses: Symptomatic relief of dysuria.
entries.cautions: Turns urine bright orange and stains contact lenses; methaemoglobinaemia and haemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

entries.mechanism: Replenishes hepatic glutathione so the toxic metabolite NAPQI can once again be neutralised.
entries.uses: Paracetamol overdose, guided by nomogram or timing rather than symptoms.
entries.cautions: Anaphylactoid infusion reactions — slow the rate, do not usually stop treatment.

entries.mechanism: Displaces the opioid from mu receptors.
entries.uses: Opioid overdose.
entries.cautions: Short half-life — the opioid can outlast it; precipitates withdrawal.

entries.mechanism: Competitively blocks the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A.
entries.uses: Benzodiazepine overdose — used sparingly.
entries.cautions: Seizures in dependent users or mixed tricyclic overdose.

entries.mechanism: Acts as an electron shuttle for NADPH methaemoglobin reductase, converting ferric iron back to ferrous so haemoglobin can carry oxygen again.
entries.uses: Methaemoglobinaemia from dapsone, prilocaine, nitrates or benzocaine; ifosfamide encephalopathy.
entries.cautions: Paradoxically causes haemolysis and worsens methaemoglobinaemia in G6PD deficiency; serotonin syndrome as it is an MAOI; turns urine and skin blue-green.

entries.mechanism: Nitrite deliberately induces methaemoglobin, which binds cyanide away from cytochrome oxidase; thiosulfate then donates sulfur so rhodanese can convert cyanide to excretable thiocyanate.
entries.uses: Cyanide poisoning.
entries.cautions: Nitrite-induced methaemoglobinaemia is itself dangerous — avoid in concurrent smoke inhalation with carbon monoxide, where hydroxocobalamin is safer.

entries.mechanism: Binds cyanide directly to form cyanocobalamin, which is renally excreted.
entries.uses: Cyanide poisoning, including smoke inhalation.
entries.cautions: Turns skin and urine deep red and interferes with colorimetric lab assays and dialysis machines.

entries.mechanism: Blocks alcohol dehydrogenase so methanol and ethylene glycol are not converted into their toxic acid metabolites.
entries.uses: Methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning.
entries.cautions: Dialysis may still be needed to clear the parent alcohol.

entries.mechanism: Chelates free iron into an excretable complex.
entries.uses: Acute iron overdose; transfusional overload.
entries.cautions: Hypotension with rapid infusion; orange-red urine; Yersinia infection risk.

entries.mechanism: Raises cardiac cAMP through its own receptor, bypassing the blocked beta receptor entirely.
entries.uses: Beta-blocker overdose with bradycardia and shock.
entries.cautions: Vomiting; very large doses required.

entries.mechanism: Atropine blocks the muscarinic effects; pralidoxime regenerates acetylcholinesterase before the bond ages.
entries.uses: Organophosphate and nerve agent poisoning.
entries.cautions: Pralidoxime must be given early; atropine is titrated to drying of secretions, not to heart rate.

entries.mechanism: Bind and inactivate digoxin, which is then excreted.
entries.uses: Severe digoxin toxicity with arrhythmia or hyperkalaemia.
entries.cautions: Digoxin assays become uninterpretable afterwards.

entries.mechanism: Idarucizumab is an antibody fragment binding dabigatran; andexanet is a decoy factor Xa that soaks up Xa inhibitors.
entries.uses: Life-threatening bleeding on a DOAC.
entries.cautions: Thrombotic risk with andexanet; very high cost.

entries.mechanism: Creates an intravascular lipid compartment that draws lipophilic drug out of tissue.
entries.uses: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity; some lipophilic overdoses.
entries.cautions: Interferes with laboratory samples; evidence outside local anaesthetics is weaker.

entries.mechanism: Raises pH and sodium load, reducing sodium-channel blockade and trapping weak acids in urine.
entries.uses: Tricyclic overdose with broad QRS; salicylate poisoning.
entries.cautions: Alkalosis, hypokalaemia, sodium load.

entries.mechanism: Adsorbs many drugs in the gut, preventing further absorption.
entries.uses: Recent significant ingestion, ideally within one hour.
entries.cautions: Does not bind iron, lithium, alcohols or strong acids and alkalis; aspiration risk if the airway is unprotected.

entries.mechanism: Displaces carbon monoxide from haemoglobin and shortens its half-life dramatically.
entries.uses: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
entries.cautions: Hyperbaric access is limited and its added benefit debated.

entries.mechanism: Binds and neutralises circulating venom toxins. It cannot reverse tissue already destroyed — which is why early administration matters more than dose.
entries.uses: Systemic envenoming by vipers, cobras, kraits and sea snakes; species and region specific.
entries.cautions: Anaphylaxis and serum sickness from foreign protein; the correct regional antivenom must be matched to the snake, since neutralisation is species-specific. Under-supplied across much of Asia and Africa.

entries.mechanism: Neutralise circulating arthropod neurotoxins.
entries.uses: Severe scorpion and funnel-web or widow spider envenoming.
entries.cautions: As snake antivenom; regional specificity essential.

entries.mechanism: Neutralises circulating diphtheria toxin before it binds tissue — antibiotics kill the organism but do nothing about toxin already released.
entries.uses: Suspected diphtheria, given on clinical suspicion without waiting for culture.
entries.cautions: Horse serum anaphylaxis and serum sickness; global supply is precarious.

entries.mechanism: Neutralises unbound tetanospasmin; toxin already internalised into nerve terminals cannot be reached.
entries.uses: Tetanus treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis in unimmunised wounds.
entries.cautions: Must be given with active immunisation at a separate site, since passive protection is temporary.

entries.drug: Rabies immunoglobulin and anti-rabies monoclonal antibodies
entries.mechanism: Infiltrated into and around the wound to neutralise virus locally before it enters peripheral nerves.
entries.uses: Category III rabies exposure, alongside vaccine.
entries.cautions: Give at a different site from the vaccine, or it neutralises the vaccine antigen too; monoclonals are replacing scarce equine and human products.

entries.mechanism: Neutralises circulating botulinum toxin.
entries.uses: Foodborne and wound botulism.
entries.cautions: Does not reverse established paralysis — recovery still requires nerve terminal regeneration.

entries.mechanism: Attenuated Mycobacterium bovis primes cell-mediated immunity.
entries.uses: Tuberculosis prevention, chiefly severe childhood forms; intravesical for bladder cancer.
entries.cautions: Local ulceration and lymphadenitis; disseminated BCG in immunodeficiency — never give to HIV-positive infants.

entries.mechanism: Replicating attenuated virus generates strong durable immunity from one or two doses.
entries.uses: Routine childhood immunisation; outbreak control.
entries.cautions: Avoid in pregnancy and significant immunosuppression; fever and rash a week later; no link to autism.

entries.class: Live attenuated and recombinant subunit vaccines
entries.mechanism: Varicella vaccine prevents primary infection; the recombinant zoster vaccine boosts waning cell-mediated immunity to prevent reactivation.
entries.uses: Chickenpox prevention; shingles prevention in older adults.
entries.cautions: Live varicella vaccine contraindicated in immunosuppression; recombinant zoster vaccine is markedly reactogenic.

entries.mechanism: Toxoids are chemically inactivated toxins that induce neutralising antibody without toxicity — immunity to the poison rather than the organism.
entries.uses: Routine childhood and pregnancy immunisation.
entries.cautions: Local reactions; acellular pertussis immunity wanes faster than whole-cell.

entries.mechanism: Oral vaccine gives mucosal immunity and interrupts transmission; inactivated gives systemic protection without reversion risk.
entries.uses: Polio eradication programmes; routine immunisation.
entries.cautions: Oral vaccine can revert to vaccine-derived poliovirus — the reason for the switch to inactivated in endemic-free regions.

entries.mechanism: Recombinant surface antigen induces protective anti-HBs.
entries.uses: Universal infant immunisation; healthcare workers; post-exposure with immunoglobulin.
entries.cautions: Non-responders need revaccination; critically important across Asia where chronic carriage is common.

entries.mechanism: Present killed virus or Vi capsular polysaccharide.
entries.uses: Travel and outbreak immunisation; endemic control.
entries.cautions: Typhoid polysaccharide gives limited duration; conjugate typhoid vaccine protects infants.

entries.mechanism: Empty capsid particles with no genome induce very high neutralising antibody titres.
entries.uses: Prevention of cervical and other HPV-related cancers.
entries.cautions: Best given before sexual debut; among the few vaccines that prevent a cancer outright.

entries.mechanism: Polysaccharide alone gives a poor T-independent response; conjugating it to a carrier protein converts it into a T-dependent response with memory, which is why conjugates work in infants.
entries.uses: Routine infant immunisation; asplenia; travel; outbreak control.
entries.cautions: Serotype replacement over time; conjugate needed for under-twos.

entries.mechanism: Reformulated annually against predicted circulating strains.
entries.uses: Annual immunisation of at-risk groups and healthcare workers.
entries.cautions: Efficacy varies with strain match; egg allergy is rarely a true contraindication now.

entries.mechanism: Mucosal immunity in the gut where the infection occurs.
entries.uses: Routine infant immunisation.
entries.cautions: Small intussusception risk; age limits on first dose.

entries.class: Inactivated or live attenuated flavivirus vaccines
entries.mechanism: Induce neutralising antibody against flavivirus envelope proteins.
entries.uses: Endemic and travel protection across South and Southeast Asia.
entries.cautions: Dengue vaccines can worsen disease in seronegative recipients through antibody-dependent enhancement — pre-vaccination serostatus screening is required.

entries.mechanism: Post-exposure immunisation outruns the virus because rabies incubates slowly in peripheral nerves.
entries.uses: Pre-exposure prophylaxis; post-exposure with immunoglobulin.
entries.cautions: One of very few vaccines given after exposure; never withhold for pregnancy or age.

entries.drug: Cholera, typhoid conjugate, mpox, Ebola, malaria and RSV vaccines
entries.mechanism: Live attenuated, inactivated, viral-vectored or recombinant depending on the pathogen.
entries.uses: Outbreak control and endemic prevention programmes.
entries.cautions: Supply and cold chain are the practical limits rather than efficacy.

entries.mechanism: Deliver mRNA instructing host cells to make one antigen, which then trains the immune system — a platform in which the antigen can be swapped in days.
entries.uses: COVID-19 prevention.
entries.cautions: Myocarditis in young men (rare); reactogenicity; demonstrated how fast vaccine development can move once a target is known.

entries.mechanism: Supplies ready-made antibody for replacement, and at high dose exerts immunomodulatory effects through Fc receptor blockade.
entries.uses: Primary immunodeficiency; Kawasaki disease; ITP; Guillain-Barré syndrome; CIDP.
entries.cautions: Infusion reactions; thrombosis, renal impairment and aseptic meningitis at high dose; a scarce plasma-derived resource.

entries.mechanism: Binds fetal RhD-positive cells before the maternal immune system can respond — preventing sensitisation rather than treating it.
entries.uses: RhD-negative mothers after delivery and sensitising events.
entries.cautions: Useless once alloimmunisation has occurred; timing is everything.

entries.mechanism: Intradermal mycobacterial protein elicits a delayed-type hypersensitivity response in previously sensitised individuals.
entries.uses: Tuberculosis infection screening.
entries.cautions: Cross-reacts with BCG and environmental mycobacteria; false negatives in immunosuppression and miliary TB.

entries.mechanism: High atomic-number iodine attenuates X-rays; there is no biological target at all — the purpose is simply to be visible.
entries.uses: CT, angiography, urography.
entries.cautions: Contrast-associated AKI in established CKD; metformin withheld because renal injury would cause it to accumulate — an interaction mediated through a third organ. Anaphylactoid reactions; iodine-induced thyroid dysfunction.

entries.mechanism: Paramagnetic gadolinium shortens T1 relaxation; chelation prevents release of the highly toxic free ion.
entries.uses: Contrast-enhanced MRI.
entries.cautions: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis in severe renal impairment — the drug's safety rests on the chelate's stability, not on any target.

entries.mechanism: Insoluble and unabsorbed, it coats the gut lumen and attenuates X-rays.
entries.uses: Fluoroscopic gastrointestinal studies.
entries.cautions: Catastrophic mediastinitis or peritonitis if it leaks through a perforation — use water-soluble contrast where perforation is suspected.

entries.mechanism: A gamma-emitting isotope bound to a carrier that determines which organ it reaches — the ligand supplies the targeting, the isotope the signal.
entries.uses: Bone, renal, cardiac, thyroid and lung imaging.
entries.cautions: Radiation exposure; pregnancy and breastfeeding restrictions.

entries.mechanism: Fluoresces under blue light, outlining corneal defects and retinal vasculature.
entries.uses: Corneal abrasion detection; retinal angiography.
entries.cautions: Stains soft contact lenses; rare anaphylaxis with intravenous use.

entries.mechanism: Disrupts microbial membranes and precipitates cytoplasmic contents; substantive, so it persists on skin for hours.
entries.uses: Skin preparation; central line care; mouthwash; umbilical cord care in neonates.
entries.cautions: Anaphylaxis, increasingly recognised and easily missed; ototoxic and neurotoxic — must be kept from the middle ear and neuraxis; alcoholic forms are a fire risk in theatre.

entries.mechanism: Releases free iodine that oxidises microbial proteins and membranes.
entries.uses: Skin and mucosal antisepsis; wound care.
entries.cautions: Thyroid dysfunction with extensive or repeated use, especially in neonates; skin staining.

entries.mechanism: Denatures microbial proteins; rapid but with no residual activity.
entries.uses: Hand hygiene between patient contacts.
entries.cautions: Ineffective against C. difficile spores and norovirus — soap and water are required there, and this is a genuine outbreak failure mode. Flammable.

entries.drug: Sodium hypochlorite / hypochlorous acid / chlorine compounds
entries.mechanism: Oxidise microbial proteins and nucleic acids; sporicidal.
entries.uses: Environmental decontamination including C. difficile and blood spills.
entries.cautions: Corrosive; toxic chlorine gas if mixed with acids or ammonia.

entries.mechanism: Cross-link microbial proteins; chloroxylenol disrupts membranes.
entries.uses: Instrument disinfection; skin and surface antisepsis.
entries.cautions: Glutaraldehyde causes occupational asthma and dermatitis — requires ventilated handling.

entries.mechanism: Blocks adenosine A1 and A2A receptors, removing the drowsiness signal; mild phosphodiesterase inhibition at high dose.
entries.uses: Alertness; neonatal apnoea of prematurity; migraine combinations.
entries.cautions: Tolerance and withdrawal headache; anxiety, tremor, insomnia; interacts with theophylline and adenosine.

entries.mechanism: Activates central nicotinic receptors, releasing dopamine in the reward pathway — the basis of its dependence.
entries.uses: Smoking cessation as replacement therapy.
entries.cautions: Strong dependence liability; the tar and combustion products, not nicotine itself, cause most smoking-related disease.

entries.mechanism: Enhances GABA-A and inhibits NMDA receptors; metabolised by alcohol dehydrogenase with zero-order kinetics at higher intakes.
entries.uses: No therapeutic use except as an alternative antidote in toxic alcohol poisoning; antiseptic.
entries.cautions: Dependence, hepatic and neurological injury, teratogenicity; additive with all CNS depressants; disulfiram-like reaction with metronidazole.

entries.mechanism: Cofactor for collagen hydroxylation and an antioxidant; enhances non-haem iron absorption.
entries.uses: Scurvy; adjunct to oral iron.
entries.cautions: Renal oxalate stones at very high dose; interferes with some glucose assays.

entries.mechanism: Cofactor for transamination and neurotransmitter synthesis.
entries.uses: Prevention of isoniazid neuropathy; some seizure syndromes; hyperemesis.
entries.cautions: Sensory peripheral neuropathy at high chronic doses — a vitamin that is genuinely neurotoxic in excess.

entries.mechanism: Incorporated into enamel as fluorapatite, which resists acid dissolution better than hydroxyapatite.
entries.uses: Dental caries prevention.
entries.cautions: Dental fluorosis with excessive childhood exposure; skeletal fluorosis at very high chronic intake.

entries.drug: Multiple micronutrient and trace element preparations
entries.mechanism: Replace cofactors required for enzymatic and structural functions.
entries.uses: Pregnancy supplementation; malabsorption; parenteral nutrition; post-bariatric surgery.
entries.cautions: Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K accumulate to toxicity; excess vitamin A is teratogenic; vitamin K interacts with warfarin.

entries.mechanism: Blocks dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin transporters, and blocks sodium channels.
entries.uses: Limited ENT topical anaesthetic use.
entries.cautions: Sympathomimetic toxidrome — dilated pupils, tachycardia, hypertension, agitation; coronary spasm and MI. Benzodiazepines are first-line; beta-blockers traditionally avoided.

entries.mechanism: Reverse the monoamine transporters, flooding the synapse with dopamine, noradrenaline and (for MDMA) serotonin.
entries.uses: Licensed amfetamine derivatives treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
entries.cautions: Sympathomimetic toxidrome; hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, hyponatraemia (MDMA), serotonin syndrome.

entries.mechanism: Profound CNS depression with a steep dose-response curve.
entries.uses: Sodium oxybate is licensed for narcolepsy with cataplexy.
entries.cautions: Abrupt deep coma with rapid spontaneous recovery; severe withdrawal syndrome; no antidote.

entries.mechanism: THC is a partial CB1 agonist; CBD acts through several non-CB1 mechanisms.
entries.uses: Nabiximols for MS spasticity; cannabidiol for specific epilepsies; nabilone for chemotherapy nausea.
entries.cautions: Psychosis risk with high-potency THC in susceptible individuals; cannabinoid hyperemesis; cognitive effects in adolescence.

entries.mechanism: Dissociative anaesthesia at subanaesthetic doses.
entries.uses: Licensed anaesthetic and antidepressant uses.
entries.cautions: Severe ulcerative cystitis with chronic heavy use, sometimes requiring cystectomy — a young person's irreversible injury.
